newsitem.title: USA: IBM takes Dow, techs higher.
newsitem.headline: IBM takes Dow, techs higher.

text.p: An earnings driven rally in shares of International Business Machines Corp powered the Dow industrials higher in mid-morning, sparking the NYSE's curbs on index arbitrage trades at 0955 EDT/1355 GMT.
IBM's impact was felt beyond the Dow as well as its better-than-forecast first quarter earnings, reported after the close of trading on Wednesday, bolstered the high techs.
The Dow was up 75 points, or 1.10 percent, at 6888 while advances led declines by 12 to five. The Nasdaq Composite was up 13 points, or 1.09 percent, at 1240.
The Dow slipped off its highs and was trading up 51 at 6864 at 1018 EDT/1418 GMT.
Alfred Goldman, technical analyst at A.G. Edwards & Sons said that IBM was adding more than 34 points to the Dow.

"It is directly helping the Dow and indirect lifting the high tech sector," Goldman said. "It's making people feel much better for the moment. People are saying 'Gee, the economy is stronger than we thought. Earnings will be climbing'."
He said that investors will now look at the darker side of the equation and wonder when the Fed will slam down the brakes by hiking interest rates again.
"How the market deals wqith this issue will determine its near-term direction," Goldman said.
Other high techs celebrated the IBM quarter, although Nasdaq, too, had slipped off its highs. It was trading up nine points, or 0.66 percent, at 1235 at 1024 EDT/1424 GMT.

Intel Corp was the most actively traded Nasdaq issue, up 1-7/8 at 148-1/8. It was followed by Cisco Systems Inc, up 1/4 at 48-7/8 in very active trading and Microsoft Corp, up 1/4 at 115-3/8. Other winners included Avid Technology Inc, up 3-7/8 at 18-7/8 and U.S. Robotics, up 2-1/8 at 49-1/8.
